title: Combination of Targeted temperature management and Thrombectomy after acute Ischemic Stroke (COTTIS-2) – a randomised controlled study
summary:
Although therapeutic cooling in animal models of stroke has consistently led to smaller infarct sizes and better outcome, this protective effect of cooling on the course of infarction has not yet been demonstrated in clinical trials. The main reasons for the failure are: cooling started too late (after only little tissue was salvageable), cooling in awake stroke patients is associated with pain and shivering, so that cooling had to be discontinued in many patients, the cooling techniques were often  associated with interventions (catheters), very different patients were included, especially patients with only very small strokes and little salvageable tissue, who have a good outcome even without additional cooling.
We have shown in a pilot study (COTTIS-1) in only patients with major stroke due to occlusion of a major cerebral artery, all of whom were in artificial coma and ventilated for mechanical clot removal via the inguinal artery, that non-invasive cooling with a nasal catheter to 35 degrees body temperature is feasible and safe, and almost all patients reached the target temperature of 35°C before reopening the vessel. This was followed by further cooling with surface mats for 6 hours, followed by slow rewarming. We did not observe  symptomatic complications and 68% of these severely affected patients had a good neurological outcome at 3 months, which is better compared to historical data. For this reason, this study (COTTIS-2) is planned to test the superiority of this cooling algorithm in patients with large stroke compared to the conventional standard without cooling.

interventions.name: Intervention: Immediately induced hypothermia to 35°C (measured esophagially) by transnasal colling with RhinoChill prior to thrombectomy followed by surface cooling for 6 hours after recanalization  in acute stroke patients with large vessel occlusion <24hours plus best medical therapy including in
Control: thrombectomy plus best medical therapy including intravenous thrombolysis in acute stroke patients with large vessel occlusion <24hours

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
o	Pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2
o	Acute ischemic stroke with NIHSS >5 
o	Indication for endovascular treatment (thrombectomy)
o	Intracranial occlusion of the M1 or M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) or internal carotid artery (ICA) or tandem occlusion on CT-angiography or MR-angiography
o	Time window:
        -Last seen normal to groin puncture < 6h: native CT or MRI-DWI with Alberta Stroke Program Early CT score (ASPECTS) >5
        -Last seen normal to groin puncture 6-24h or unknown time window: significant mismatch imaging according to the eligibility criteria of the DEFUSE-3 trial:
                        - Infarct core <70ml (DWI oder CBF<30% of contralateral site)
                        - Penumbra > 15ml (Tmax >6sec)
                        - Ratio penumbra/core >1.8
o	with or without iv thrombolysis with rtPA
Exclusion criteria:
o	Patients with an intranasal obstruction that prevents complete insertion of the nasal cannula should not be treated with the RhinoChill system.
o	Known severe hemorrhagic diathesis (International Normalized Ratio (INR) >3.0, partial thromboplastin time (PTT) > 70s, platelet count < 50.000/μl)
o	Brain trauma or neurovascular surgery/intervention <3 months
o	Severe infection
o	Pregnant women or women of childbearing potential (women of childbearing potential with negative pregnancy test may be included)
o	Known cerebral vasculitis
o	Proof of bleeding in cerebral CT or MRI (cerebral microbleeds in MRI [hypertensive or in the context of cerebral amyloid angiopathy] is permitted).
o	Life expectancy < 6 months
